title: Scientific capstone: an auditable offline modeling report
outcome: Execute a complete synthetic modeling workflow from typed CSV to a source-identified decision record, exact numerical checks and an accessible Plotly report.
key_terms: Written checks on identifiers, types, finiteness and timing that reject an input file before any model is fitted.
The time when a feature or label became known, which must precede its use for the row to be valid.
A procedure fixed before scoring, such as choosing the lowest development error with ties broken by candidate order.
Rows reserved for a single final evaluation after selection and never used to choose the penalty.
Recorded source identity, settings and split counts that link a reported result to its exact inputs.
approach: `analyze` reads the eight-row `SENSOR_CSV` with declared types, runs `validate_sensor` for row count, unique ids, finite values, known splits, feature and label availability and split counts of 4, 2 and 2, then fits ridge lines on the four training rows. It selects the penalty by development MSE and writes a memo with the fixture SHA-256.

exercises.title: Audit the grain
exercises.task: Explain what one row and one ID represent.
exercises.expected: One synthetic prediction record with declared availability evidence.
exercises.answer: The eight-row contract fixes grain and denominators; repeated entities in real data would need additional grouping.
exercises.why: Each row has a unique id such as `s01` and represents one synthetic prediction with its own feature and label availability dates.
exercises.wrong: Treating the ids as entities that may repeat would require grouping rules that this fixture does not define.
exercises.verify: The reference duplicates `id[8]` and asserts `validate_sensor` throws `ArgumentError`.

exercises.title: Reproduce the selection
exercises.task: Compare development errors for the four fixed penalties.
exercises.hint: Do not inspect final outcomes to choose candidates.
exercises.answer: The declared rule chooses the minimum development MSE in fixed candidate order.
exercises.why: The training rows are the same x and y values as lesson julia-021, so the four penalties give the same development errors and penalty 2 wins.
exercises.wrong: Choosing by final error reuses the assessment rows for selection and makes the reported final MSE optimistic.

exercises.title: Verify final arithmetic
exercises.task: Compute residuals for predictions 90/7 and 103/7 against 13 and 15.
exercises.hint: Square and average the two errors.
exercises.answer: This independent rational calculation verifies the reported floating result.
exercises.why: Predictions 90/7 and 103/7 against 13 and 15 leave residuals -1/7 and -2/7, whose squares 1/49 and 4/49 average to 5/98.
exercises.wrong: Averaging the absolute residuals gives 3/14, a different metric from the mean squared error stored in the memo.
exercises.verify: Example A asserts `result.memo["final_mse"] ≈ 5/98`; compute the fractions by hand beside it.

exercises.title: Inject information leakage
exercises.task: Move a feature availability date after its prediction date.
exercises.expected: The data validator rejects the fixture.
exercises.answer: A future-known feature cannot enter the historical decision under the declared contract.
exercises.why: Setting row 7's feature date to 2024-02-01, after its prediction date 2024-01-07, breaks `feature_available_at .<= prediction_at`.
exercises.wrong: Checking only that dates parse lets a future feature enter the model and makes the historical evaluation impossible in practice.
exercises.verify: The reference asserts `ArgumentError` for that change and for a label date after the 2024-01-10 cutoff.

exercises.title: Inspect accessible evidence
exercises.task: Compare each Plotly table row with its plotted observation and prediction.
exercises.expected: The values and IDs must match exactly.
exercises.hint: The chart is a view of the same final data.
exercises.answer: Descriptions explain scope; exact tables support inspection without relying on visual position.
exercises.why: The Plotly table and markers come from the same `final` rows and `predictions`, so ids, observations and predictions must match exactly.
exercises.wrong: Reading values off the chart by eye introduces rounding and misses an id paired with the wrong row.
exercises.verify: Compare each table row with `result.final` and `result.predictions` programmatically.

exercises.title: Write the decision memo
exercises.task: State what passes and what evidence is still missing.
exercises.expected: Synthetic computation passes; deployment is not justified.
exercises.hint: Mention small final sample and selection history.
exercises.answer: Require representative sampling, uncertainty, domain validation and monitoring before making a deployment claim.
exercises.why: The synthetic workflow passes all checks, but two final rows and a hand-built fixture cannot support a deployment decision.
exercises.wrong: Writing that the model is ready because the final MSE is small ignores sample size, selection history and domain validity.
exercises.verify: Confirm the memo's decision text says deployment evidence is insufficient and that `fixture_sha256` matches `bytes2hex(sha256(SENSOR_CSV))`.
